label: Event-level detection with delayed labels
summary: A runnable reference for scoring individual events (fraud, abuse, default, churn, risk) with point-in-time features, labels that arrive late, a chronological split and a calibrated baseline against a regularised boosted model.
runtime: Python 3.11+ with numpy, pandas, scikit-learn, scipy and pytest (about 10 seconds)
run: python -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate && pip install -r requirements.txt
expected: make_data.py prints about 188,000 events with a positive rate near 0.36%. baseline.py reports the calibrated logistic baseline at recall 0.74 and PR-AUC 0.69 at a 0.5% false-positive rate, and the boosted challenger at 0.76 and 0.75. pytest reports 5 passed.

files.purpose: Synthetic event stream with genuine bursts, shared-group attacks, quiet takeovers and delayed labels
Point-in-time window counts, shared-group fan-out and matured counterparty rates
Chronological split, calibrated baseline, boosted challenger and the metric report
Executable gates: determinism, leakage, window boundaries, matured labels and thresholds

synthetic.description: About 190,000 events over 120 days for 2,500 entities with genuine bursts, flash events at a counterparty, fast attacks through a shared group, quiet takeovers on the entity's own group, and labels that only arrive 7-21 days late.
knobs: positive_entity_rate: share of entities that are compromised (default 3%)
n_flash_sales: genuine counterparty-level spikes that stress false positives
n_entities, days, n_counterparties: scale and history length
seed: identical seed gives an identical stream

slots.meaning: count and sum of the entity's events in the last minute, hour and day, closed strictly before the decision time
distinct entities seen on the same group in the last 24 hours
first time this entity is seen on this group
share of confirmed positives at the counterparty, using only labels that had arrived by decision time
value compared with the entity's own normal

data.threshold: pytest -k 'deterministic or matured' passes; positive rate between 0.2% and 1.2%
data.how: Run pytest in the kit directory

features.threshold: Deleting all rows after day 60 changes no feature of any earlier row (maximum absolute difference 0)

baseline.metric: Recall at a 0.5% false-positive rate and PR-AUC
baseline.threshold: Recall at least 0.60 and PR-AUC at least 0.55 (the kit reaches 0.74 and 0.69)

challenger.metric: PR-AUC of the challenger against the baseline
challenger.threshold: At least 0.95 times the baseline's PR-AUC (the kit reaches 1.08 times); on real data the lower bound of a 95% entity-level bootstrap interval of the lift is above zero

tests.pass: No feature of any past row changes when all later rows are deleted
A 61-second-old event is outside a 1-minute window and the current event is never counted
Every training label arrived before the first test row
Baseline recall at 0.5% FPR at least 0.60 and PR-AUC at least 0.55; challenger PR-AUC at least 0.95 times baseline

lessons.trap: Training on labels that had not matured
lessons.evidence: Labels arrive 7-21 days late, so the kit trains only on rows whose label arrived before the cut-off and leaves a maturity gap before the test period.

lessons.trap: A window that includes the future
lessons.evidence: The future-truncation test fails if any feature of an earlier row changes when later rows are deleted.
With a 0.36% positive rate a model that always says no is 99.6% accurate; the kit reports recall at a fixed false-positive rate and PR-AUC instead.

lessons.trap: An unregularised boosted model on a few hundred positives
lessons.evidence: An unregularised depth-4 boosted model scored PR-AUC 0.33 against 0.69 for the baseline; strong regularisation brought it to 0.75.

target: A row is positive when the outcome is later confirmed (a confirmed fraud, a default, a churn). A positive's label arrives 7 to 21 days after the event; a negative is only confirmed after the full maturity window.

headline.baseline: recall 0.74 and PR-AUC 0.69 at a 0.5% false-positive rate
